docs.title: vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input
docs.text:
vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input is an MkDocs plugin. After MkDocs has built your site, the plugin reads each rendered HTML page, cuts out the part you choose, and writes it to a new Markdown file together with the YAML front matter of the original source page. These new files are called cousin files. They live in a separate directory, stage/ by default, and mirror the layout of your docs/ directory.

The package also installs a command-line tool, mkdocs-output-as-input, that applies the same extraction to a single HTML file outside of an MkDocs build.

docs.title: What goes in and what comes out
docs.text:
Take one source page, docs/index.md:

---
title: My Page
author: Jane Doe
---

# My Page

This is my content with **markdown**.

With the Material theme and this configuration:

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: article.md-content__inner
      target_tag: section

mkdocs build writes the normal site into site/. The plugin then writes stage/index.md:

---
author: Jane Doe
title: My Page
---

<section class="md-content__inner md-typeset">
<h1 id="my-page">My Page</h1>
<p>This is my content with <strong>markdown</strong>.</p>
</section>

The front matter comes from the source file. The body is the HTML that MkDocs and the theme produced, after every Markdown extension and plugin ran. The extracted <article> element was renamed to <section>; its attributes were kept.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to feed MkDocs-rendered content into another static site generator or a CMS that reads Markdown files with front matter.
  • You want the page body without the theme's header, navigation and footer.
  • You want a copy of each page's rendered HTML next to its metadata, for archiving or further processing.

docs.title: Command-line tool
docs.text: The mkdocs-output-as-input command applies the plugin's extraction to one HTML file, without running MkDocs. Use it to test a selector against a page you already built, or to convert single files in a script.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
mkdocs-output-as-input [-h] [--version] {process} ...

mkdocs-output-as-input process [-h] [--html-element HTML_ELEMENT]
                               [--target-tag TARGET_TAG]
                               [--no-frontmatter] [--preserve-links]
                               [--minify] [--prettify] [-v]
                               input output

The tool has one subcommand, process. Running the tool without a subcommand prints the help text and exits with status 1.

docs.title: process arguments
docs.text:
Argument Default Effect input required Path to the HTML file to read output required Path of the Markdown file to write; missing parent directories are created --html-element HTML_ELEMENT main CSS selector for the content to extract; repeat the option to give several selectors --target-tag TARGET_TAG article Tag name for the renamed element or for the wrapper around several elements --no-frontmatter off Do not look for front matter and do not write any --preserve-links off Prefix root-relative href and src values with . --minify off Remove line breaks and double spaces from the HTML --prettify off Indent the HTML with BeautifulSoup's prettify() -v, --verbose off Log at debug level, with module, function and line number

Global options:

Option Effect -h, --help Show help and exit --version Print mkdocs-output-as-input <version> and exit

docs.title: Where the front matter comes from
docs.text: An HTML file has no YAML front matter of its own. The process command looks for a Markdown file with the same path as input but with the .md extension. For site/guide/index.html it checks site/guide/index.md. If that file exists and starts with a front matter block, the block is copied into the output. If the file does not exist, the output has no front matter.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Prerequisites: an HTML page built by MkDocs with the built-in mkdocs theme, page.html, and next to it page.md with this content:

---
title: My Page
---
# x

  1. Run the command with a selector that matches the theme's content area:

    mkdocs-output-as-input process page.html out.md --html-element 'div[role=main]'

    The tool logs Processing file and Successfully wrote output file.

  2. Read the result:

    ---
title: My Page
---

<div class="col-md-9" role="main">
<h1 id="my-page">My Page</h1>
...

The front matter came from page.md; the HTML came from page.html.

docs.title: Differences from the plugin
docs.text:
The command shares its approach with the plugin but is a separate implementation. Three details differ:

  • Renaming a single element. The command renames the element to --target-tag only when the selector is a plain tag name that equals the element's own tag, for example --html-element main on a <main> element. In the example above the selector div[role=main] is not a tag name, so the <div> keeps its tag. The plugin renames in that case.
  • Minifying. --minify removes line breaks and replaces double spaces with single spaces. The plugin's minify option also removes whitespace between tags.
  • Front matter source. The command reads the .md file next to the HTML file. The plugin reads the original source page from docs_dir.

Several matched elements are wrapped in one --target-tag element, as in the plugin.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
Status Meaning 0 The output file was written 1 No subcommand was given, --minify and --prettify were both given, no element matched, or reading or writing a file failed

On failure the tool logs the reason, for example No elements found followed by Command failed.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure the plugin under plugins in mkdocs.yml. All options are optional.

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      stage_dir: stage
      html_element: main
      target_tag: article
      include_frontmatter: true
      preserve_links: false
      minify: false
      prettify: false
      verbose: false

The block above lists every option with its default value.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Type Default Effect stage_dir string stage Directory for cousin files, relative to the parent of docs_dir html_element string or list of strings main CSS selector or selectors for the content to extract target_tag string article Tag name for the extracted element in the output include_frontmatter boolean true Write the source page's YAML front matter at the top of the cousin file preserve_links boolean false Prefix root-relative href and src values with . minify boolean false Remove line breaks and whitespace between tags prettify boolean false Indent the HTML with BeautifulSoup's prettify() verbose boolean false Log extra details about each page

MkDocs checks the type of each option when it loads the configuration and stops if a value has the wrong type.

docs.title: stage_dir
docs.text:
The plugin creates the stage directory at <parent of docs_dir>/<stage_dir>. With the usual layout, where mkdocs.yml and docs/ sit side by side, the stage directory is a sibling of docs/ and site/.

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      stage_dir: processed

The plugin creates only the last directory in the path. A nested value such as build/markdown works only if build/ already exists; otherwise the build stops with FileNotFoundError. See Troubleshooting.

The plugin does not empty the stage directory before writing. Files from earlier builds stay there until you delete them.

docs.title: html_element
docs.text:
A CSS selector, or a list of CSS selectors, that picks the content to extract from each rendered page. Selectors are evaluated with BeautifulSoup's select(). If a selector matches nothing, the plugin tries it once more as a plain tag name with find().

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: article.md-content__inner

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element:
        - h1
        - div.md-content

What ends up in the output depends on how many elements match in total:

  • One element. It is written as-is. If html_element is a single string, the element's tag is renamed to target_tag unless html_element already equals target_tag. The element's attributes are kept. If html_element is a list, the element keeps its original tag.
  • Several elements. This happens when a list has more than one matching selector, or when one selector matches several elements. The plugin creates a new, attribute-free target_tag element and moves all matches into it, in selector order.
  • No elements. The plugin logs No matching elements found and writes no cousin file for that page.

Because the rename rule compares the option value with target_tag, a single string selector such as .content or div[role=main] is also renamed. html_element: article with the default target_tag: article keeps the tag unchanged.

docs.title: target_tag
docs.text:
The tag name used for the renamed element or for the wrapper around several elements.

plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: main
      target_tag: section

With this configuration, <main class="md-main">…</main> becomes <section class="md-main">…</section>.

docs.title: include_frontmatter
docs.text:
When true, the cousin file starts with the source page's front matter, followed by a blank line. When false, the cousin file contains only the HTML.

The plugin recognises front matter only when the source file starts with a line that is exactly --- and the block ends with another line that is exactly ---. It parses the block with yaml.safe_load and writes it back with yaml.safe_dump. As a result:

  • Keys are written in alphabetical order.
  • Lists and mappings are written in block style.
  • Comments and the original formatting are not kept.

If the block is not valid YAML, the plugin logs Failed to parse frontmatter and treats the page as having no front matter. A page with no front matter, or with an empty block, gets no front matter in its cousin file.

docs.title: preserve_links
docs.text:
When true, the plugin looks at every <a>, <img>, <link> and <script> element inside the extracted content. Any href or src value that starts with / but not with // gets a . prefix, so /guide/ becomes ./guide/. Protocol-relative URLs (//example.com/…), absolute URLs and relative URLs are not changed.

MkDocs normally writes relative links, so this option only changes links that are root-relative in the rendered HTML, for example links written as /path in raw HTML inside your Markdown.

docs.title: minify and prettify
docs.text:
These options change the formatting of the HTML part of the cousin file:

  • minify: true removes all line breaks, collapses each run of whitespace to one space and removes whitespace between a > and the next <.
  • prettify: true passes the element through BeautifulSoup's prettify(), which puts each tag and text node on its own indented line.
  • With both false, the HTML is written as BeautifulSoup serialises it, which is close to what the theme produced.

You cannot enable both. If you do, the plugin raises ValueError: Cannot use both 'minify' and 'prettify' options when the build starts, in the on_config step, and the build stops.

docs.title: verbose
docs.text:
When true, the plugin logs Plugin initialized with the site and docs directories, the resolved configuration, one Captured source file message per page with its front matter keys, and one Created cousin file message per written file.

The plugin logs through loguru, which writes to standard error in its own format, separate from MkDocs' own log lines.

docs.title: Configuration example for a pipeline
docs.text:
plugins:
  - search
  - output-as-input:
      stage_dir: content
      html_element: article.md-content__inner
      target_tag: div
      include_frontmatter: true
      prettify: true

This writes one Markdown file per page into content/, each with the original front matter and an indented <div> holding the Material theme's article body.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Bug reports and pull requests are welcome at github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input. For larger changes, open an issue first to discuss the approach.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Contents src/mkdocs_output_as_input/plugin.py The MkDocs plugin, OutputAsInputPlugin src/mkdocs_output_as_input/cli.py The mkdocs-output-as-input command src/mkdocs_output_as_input/__init__.py Exports OutputAsInputPlugin and __version__ tests/ pytest test suite, including an end-to-end MkDocs build in test_integration.py src_docs/md/ Source of this documentation site src_docs/mkdocs.yml Documentation site configuration docs/ Built documentation site, served by GitHub Pages; do not edit by hand scripts/ Helper scripts for setup, tests and builds

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python 3.12 or newer and uv.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input
cd vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input

  2. Create a virtual environment and install the package with its development extras:

    uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

  3. Install the pre-commit hooks:

    uv run pre-commit install

scripts/dev-setup.sh performs the same steps.

docs.title: Run the tests and checks
docs.text:
Run the test suite:

uv run pytest

scripts/test.sh runs the full set of checks in this order: ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy src, and pytest with coverage. The coverage configuration in pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 90.

The pre-commit configuration also runs pyupgrade, black, codespell and the standard whitespace, YAML and TOML checks.

The GitHub Actions workflow ci.yml runs the tests on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.12 and 3.13, a MkDocs compatibility job, and a lint job with ruff, black and mypy.

docs.title: Build the package and the documentation
docs.text:
The root build.sh builds both:

./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only
./build.sh package    # package only
  • The documentation is built by src_docs/build.sh with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme, in strict mode, from src_docs/md/ into docs/. src_docs/build.sh serve starts a live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000.
  • The package is built with uv build into dist/ and checked with twine check.

The version number comes from the latest Git tag through hatch-vcs. At build time it is written to src/mkdocs_output_as_input/_version.py, which is not committed. A checkout without that file reports the version 0.0.0+unknown.

After a push to main that changes src_docs/, the docs.yml workflow rebuilds docs/ and commits the result.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
publish.sh makes a release:

  1. gitnextver commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes it.
  2. ./build.sh package builds the package from that tag.
  3. uv publish uploads dist/* to PyPI. This needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN or another uv publish credential.

Pushing a v* tag also starts the release.yml workflow, which builds the package, uploads it to PyPI through trusted publishing (skipping files that already exist), and creates a GitHub release.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text: Write documentation pages in src_docs/md/. Describe only behaviour that the code has, use sentence-case headings, and put commands, paths and option names in code style. Run ./build.sh docs before you open a pull request; the build must pass in strict mode.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Each example shows a configuration and the result it produces. The selectors were checked against MkDocs 1.6.1 with the built-in mkdocs theme and with Material for MkDocs.

docs.title: Built-in mkdocs theme
docs.text:
The built-in theme puts page content in <div class="col-md-9" role="main"> and has no <main> element.

site_name: Demo
plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: "div[role=main]"

Result for a page with the heading # Setup:

<article class="col-md-9" role="main">
<h1 id="setup">Setup</h1>
...
</article>

The <div> is renamed to <article> because target_tag defaults to article. To keep it a <div>, set target_tag: div.

docs.title: Material for MkDocs: article body only
docs.text:
site_name: Demo
theme: material
plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: article.md-content__inner
      target_tag: section
      stage_dir: out

Result in out/index.md for a page with title and author in its front matter:

---
author: Jane Doe
title: My Page
---

<section class="md-content__inner md-typeset">
<h1 id="my-page">My Page</h1>
<p>This is my content with <strong>markdown</strong>.</p>
</section>

With Material and the default html_element: main, the plugin extracts <main class="md-main">, which contains the navigation and table-of-contents sidebars as well as the article. Use article.md-content__inner when you only want the page body.

docs.title: Several selectors in one file
docs.text:
plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element:
        - h1
        - div.admonition
      target_tag: div

For each page, every <h1> and every element with the class admonition is moved into one new <div>, headings first, then admonitions. The wrapper has no attributes. If a page has only one match in total, that element is written on its own and keeps its original tag.

docs.title: HTML only, no front matter
docs.text:
plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: article.md-content__inner
      include_frontmatter: false
      minify: true

Each cousin file holds a single line of HTML with no front matter block. This suits tools that read HTML fragments and ignore the file extension.

docs.title: Readable HTML for review
docs.text:
plugins:
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: article.md-content__inner
      prettify: true

Every tag and text node is placed on its own indented line, which makes diffs between builds easier to read. Do not combine prettify with minify.

docs.title: Feeding another site generator
docs.text:
The plugin writes plain files and runs nothing else, so you chain the next tool after mkdocs build:

mkdocs build
ls stage/

Point the next tool at the stage directory. To write straight into another project's content folder, set stage_dir to a path relative to the parent of docs_dir, for example ../other-site/content. The parent folder, ../other-site, must already exist; the plugin creates only the last directory.

The cousin files keep the .md extension but contain HTML after the front matter. Most Markdown processors pass raw HTML through unchanged; check that your target tool does.

docs.title: Testing a selector with the CLI
docs.text:
Before you change mkdocs.yml, try a selector on one built page:

mkdocs build
mkdocs-output-as-input process site/index.html /tmp/index-test.md \
  --html-element article.md-content__inner --target-tag section
cat /tmp/index-test.md

If the selector matches nothing, the command logs No elements found and exits with status 1. The CLI and the plugin differ in how they rename a single element; see Command-line tool.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The plugin class is OutputAsInputPlugin in mkdocs_output_as_input/plugin.py. It subclasses MkDocs' BasePlugin and uses three MkDocs events. Front matter and rendered HTML exist at different times during a build, so the plugin collects them in separate steps and combines them at the end.

docs.title: 1. on_config: remember the directories
docs.text: When the build starts, the plugin stores site_dir and docs_dir from the MkDocs configuration. It then checks that minify and prettify are not both enabled and raises ValueError if they are.

docs.title: 2. on_page_read_source: capture the front matter
docs.text:
MkDocs calls this event once per page, before it reads the page's Markdown. The plugin:

  1. Opens the source file at the page's absolute source path and reads it as UTF-8.
  2. If the text starts with --- followed by a line break, looks for the next line that is exactly --- and parses the text between them with yaml.safe_load.
  3. Stores the parsed front matter and the source path in a dictionary keyed by the page's path relative to docs_dir, for example guide/setup.md.
  4. Returns None, so MkDocs reads and renders the page normally.

The plugin does not change the page content. The rendered HTML does not exist yet at this point.

docs.title: 3. on_post_build: write the cousin files
docs.text: MkDocs calls this event once, after it has written every page into site_dir. The plugin creates the stage directory, <parent of docs_dir>/<stage_dir>, and then handles each recorded page.

docs.title: Finding the HTML file
docs.text:
For a source path such as guide/setup.md, the plugin tries these files in site_dir, in order:

Source path First try Second try guide/setup.md guide/setup/index.html guide/setup.html index.md index/index.html index.html README.md at the root of docs_dir, any case index.html README.html

The first column of tries matches use_directory_urls: true, the MkDocs default; the second matches use_directory_urls: false and index.md pages. If neither file exists, the plugin logs No HTML output found and skips the page.

docs.title: Extracting the content
docs.text:
1. The HTML file is parsed with BeautifulSoup's built-in html.parser.
  2. Each selector from html_element is run with select(). If it matches nothing, the plugin tries find() with the selector as a tag name.
  3. All matches are collected. One match is used directly and renamed to target_tag when html_element is a single string. Several matches are moved into a new target_tag element.
  4. If preserve_links is on, root-relative href and src values get a . prefix.

docs.title: Writing the output
docs.text:
The cousin file path is <stage_dir>/<source path>, so guide/setup.md becomes stage/guide/setup.md. Missing subdirectories inside the stage directory are created. The file contains, in this order:

  1. If include_frontmatter is on and the page had front matter: a --- line, the front matter written by yaml.safe_dump, another --- line and a blank line.
  2. The extracted HTML, minified, prettified or as serialised by BeautifulSoup.
  3. A final line break.

docs.title: Errors and the summary line
docs.text:
An error while processing one page is logged as Failed to process file and counted. The plugin moves on to the next page; one bad page does not stop the build. After the last page, the plugin logs Post-build processing complete with the counts processed, failed and total, and the elapsed time.

Pages that were skipped because no HTML file or no matching element was found are counted as processed, because skipping is not an error.

docs.title: Pages the plugin sees
docs.text: The plugin only knows about pages that pass through on_page_read_source. These are the Markdown pages MkDocs builds. Static files that MkDocs copies unchanged, such as images or HTML files in docs_dir, get no cousin file.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Both the plugin and the CLI log with loguru. The plugin uses loguru's default sink, which writes to standard error. Its messages appear alongside, but separately from, MkDocs' own INFO and WARNING lines. Messages that loguru logs as warnings are not MkDocs warnings, so mkdocs build --strict does not fail because of them.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer. The package declares requires-python = ">=3.12" and uses Python 3.12 syntax.
  • MkDocs 1.6.0 or newer.

Installing the package also installs its runtime dependencies:

Package Minimum version Used for mkdocs 1.6.0 Plugin base class and configuration options beautifulsoup4 4.12.0 Parsing the rendered HTML and selecting elements pyyaml 6.0 Reading and writing YAML front matter loguru 0.7.0 Log messages from the plugin and the CLI

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
Install the package into the same environment that runs MkDocs.

With uv:

uv pip install vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input

With pip:

pip install vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input

If you run MkDocs through uvx, add the package with --with:

uvx --from mkdocs --with vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input mkdocs build

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input
cd vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input
uv pip install -e .

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
1. Print the version of the command-line tool:

    mkdocs-output-as-input --version

    The output has the form mkdocs-output-as-input <version>.

  2. Confirm that MkDocs can find the plugin. The package registers the plugin under the name output-as-input in the mkdocs.plugins entry-point group. If MkDocs cannot find it, mkdocs build stops with an error that names the missing plugin.

docs.title: Names at a glance
docs.text: What Name PyPI package vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input Plugin name in mkdocs.yml output-as-input Python import package mkdocs_output_as_input Plugin class mkdocs_output_as_input.plugin.OutputAsInputPlugin Command-line tool mkdocs-output-as-input

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walk-through enables the plugin on a small MkDocs project and checks the result.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The package is installed in the environment that runs MkDocs. See Installation.
  • You have an MkDocs project with mkdocs.yml at its root and pages in docs/.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Find out which HTML element holds the page content in your theme. The default selector is main, which does not suit every theme:

    Theme Selector for the page content mkdocs (the built-in default) div[role=main] material article.md-content__inner

    The built-in mkdocs theme has no <main> element, so with the default selector the plugin finds nothing. In Material, main matches <main class="md-main">, which also contains the navigation sidebars.

  2. Add the plugin to mkdocs.yml. For the built-in theme:

    site_name: Demo
plugins:
  - search
  - output-as-input:
      html_element: "div[role=main]"

    Keep any plugins you already use. When you list plugins: yourself, MkDocs no longer adds search automatically, so list it if you want it.

  3. Build the site:

    mkdocs build

    MkDocs writes site/ as usual. The plugin then logs Creating stage directory and, at the end, Post-build processing complete with the number of processed and failed pages.

  4. Look at the cousin files. They are in stage/, next to docs/:

    my-project/
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md
│   └── guide/
│       └── setup.md
├── site/
├── stage/
│   ├── index.md
│   └── guide/
│       └── setup.md
└── mkdocs.yml

    Each file in stage/ has the same relative path as its source page.

docs.title: What a cousin file contains
docs.text:
Source docs/guide/setup.md:

# Setup

See [home](../index.md).

Cousin file stage/guide/setup.md, built with the mkdocs theme and html_element: "div[role=main]":

<article class="col-md-9" role="main">
<h1 id="setup">Setup</h1>
<p>See <a href="../../">home</a>.</p></article>

The source has no front matter, so the cousin file has none. The <div> was renamed to <article>, the default target_tag. The link is the rendered link that MkDocs wrote into site/, relative to the page's HTML location, not to the source Markdown.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Change the output directory, the element and the output tag in Configuration.
  • Add stage/ to your .gitignore if you do not want to commit the cousin files.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: The plugin logs through loguru to standard error. Turn on verbose: true for one message per captured page and per written file. The messages quoted below are the exact texts the plugin logs.

docs.title: No matching elements found
docs.text:
Cause. None of the selectors in html_element matched anything in the rendered page, so no cousin file was written for that page. The most common case is the default selector main with the built-in mkdocs theme, which has no <main> element.

Fix.

  1. Open one page from site/ in a browser or text editor and find the element that wraps the content.
  2. Set html_element to a selector for it, for example div[role=main] for the built-in theme or article.md-content__inner for Material.
  3. Test the selector on that page with mkdocs-output-as-input process site/index.html /tmp/test.md --html-element "<selector>".
  4. Run mkdocs build again.

These messages do not fail mkdocs build --strict, because loguru messages are not MkDocs warnings. Check the build output for them, or count the cousin files.

docs.title: No HTML output found
docs.text:
Cause. The plugin could not find the HTML file for a page. It looks for <page>/index.html and then <page>.html in site_dir. A plugin or theme that writes pages to other locations, or a page whose path contains .md more than once, can cause this.

Fix. Run with verbose: true, note the expected_path in the message, and compare it with the files in site/.

docs.title: FileNotFoundError for the stage directory
docs.text:
Cause. stage_dir has more than one path component, for example build/markdown, and the parent directory build/ does not exist. The plugin creates only the last directory of the path.

Fix. Create the parent directory before the build, or use a single directory name:

mkdir -p build
mkdocs build

docs.title: ValueError: Cannot use both 'minify' and 'prettify' options
docs.text:
Cause. Both options are true. The plugin checks this when the build starts.

Fix. Set at least one of them to false.

docs.title: The cousin file has no front matter
docs.text:
Check these in order:

  1. include_frontmatter is not set to false.
  2. The source file starts with --- on the very first line, with nothing before it, not even a blank line or a byte-order mark.
  3. The block ends with a line that is exactly ---.
  4. The block is valid YAML. If it is not, the plugin logs Failed to parse frontmatter.
  5. The block is not empty.

docs.title: The front matter looks different from the source
docs.text: The plugin parses the block and writes it again with yaml.safe_dump. Keys are sorted alphabetically, comments are dropped and formatting is normalised. The values are the same.

docs.title: Old files remain in the stage directory
docs.text:
The plugin overwrites cousin files but never deletes files. If you delete or rename a source page, its old cousin file stays. Remove the stage directory before a clean build:

rm -rf stage
mkdocs build

docs.title: The extracted element has the wrong tag
docs.text: With a single string in html_element, the plugin renames the matched element to target_tag, even when the selector is a class or attribute selector. Set target_tag to the tag you want to keep, for example target_tag: div. With a list in html_element and one match, the element keeps its own tag.

docs.title: Links point to the wrong place
docs.text: The HTML in a cousin file is the HTML from site/, so relative links are relative to the page's location in site/, for example ../../ for guide/setup/index.html. They are not relative to the cousin file in the stage directory. preserve_links only changes links that start with a single /.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: Search or open an issue at github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-output-as-input/issues. Include your mkdocs.yml, the theme, and the output of a build with verbose: true.
